chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade me from wearing the clothes of notoriety, and I am not saying he forbade you all from wearing the saffron-dyed and vibrant-colored garments.'

key_terms.الْمُعَصْفَرُ: Saffron-dyed garment — cloth dyed with safflower (usfur), producing a yellow or orange hue; permitted in general for believers
key_terms.الْمُفْدَمُ: Vibrant-colored garment — intensely or deeply dyed cloth; permitted in general for believers
key_terms.ثِيَابُ الشُّهْرَةِ: Clothes of notoriety — garments worn to draw attention, achieve fame, or signal social status; prohibited because they foster pride and ostentation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the Prophet's prohibition on wearing clothes of notoriety?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) distinguishes between a personal prohibition addressed to him by the Prophet (SAWW) — namely the wearing of ثياب الشهرة (clothes of notoriety or ostentation) — and a general ruling that does not prohibit all believers from wearing dyed or vibrant-colored garments. This hadith reveals that certain prophetic directives were specific to individuals based on their station, particularly the Imam's role as a public leader whose dress had to reflect humility and avoid drawing attention for the wrong reasons. The nuanced distinction here reflects the Shia jurisprudential tradition of differentiating between rulings particular to the Prophet's household and those applying to the general community.
